canonical_question: Is the 'large ductility' of the N-2 HEA maintained during cyclic loading at the high temperatures where the damping peak occurs?

question_variants.question: Is the 'large ductility' of the N-2 HEA maintained during cyclic loading at the high temperatures where the damping peak occurs?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text confirms large ductility is retained at room temperature and mentions high-temperature damping peaks. It does not provide data on ductility maintenance specifically under cyclic loading at the high temperatures where damping peaks occur.

answers.answer: The text states that the large ductility of the N-2 HEA is retained, but it does not specify whether this ductility is maintained during cyclic loading at the high temperatures (~800 K) where the damping peak occurs.
answers.measurement_outcome: Large ductility retained (context unspecified as cyclic or static)
answers.boundary_limitation: No data on cyclic loading performance at peak damping temperatures.
evidence_spans: It is also important to note that the peak temperature of damping in the current Snoek-type high-damping HEAs is approximately 100 K higher than that in traditional high-damping alloys ( [11] , [12] , [31] – [42] ).

Because of the high configuration entropy and severely distorted lattices of HEAs ( [50] ), atomic position switches of interstitials in these matrices are impeded by the high atomic-scale distortion fields ( [51] ).
This effect gives rise to the high activation temperatures and barrier energies for the interstitial reorientation steps and the resulting high-temperature damping capability.

source_evidence_spans: the large ductility of the nitrogen-containing N-2 HEA is retained
